Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the inherited rollout/notes, both required wake visual views, and the fish-control shelf. Then I’ll implement and validate one candidate, keeping candidate reasoning and the reusable evidence lesson in their mandated files.

The workspace is an inherited later iteration, not the common naïve seed. I’m checking the stagnation history now to determine whether the bookshelf consultation is mandatory under the three-iteration trigger; I’ll consult it regardless because the user explicitly requested that protocol.

All four sampled rollouts are captures, so there is no semantic failure sheet in this sample. I’ll use the best-score v24 rollout as the strong finite example and the worst-score moment-gated v31 rollout as the informative negative comparison, while explicitly retaining the “no sampled failure” limitation. Both confirm direct uniform still-water initialization.

The visual comparison shows the same useful topology in both: self-propelled target approach, a coherent alternating wake in top-down and oblique views, and a late upward/left course bend into capture. The sheets do not visually support wholesale carrier replacement. The negative sample’s distinctions are terminal diagnostics rather than a different trajectory class, so the next change should be a compact state selector on the existing posterior relief mechanism. I’m consulting the shelf now; this is influencing architecture, so I’ll record the required transfer block before editing the policy.

I’m using the bookshelf’s asymmetric-flapping primitive only at the mechanism level: the existing body-frame course residual will authorize bounded relief of one observed posterior half-cycle, while the validated carrier and mean C-bend remain unchanged. I’m recording that hypothesis and its falsification boundary now, before touching the policy as required.

The candidate now replaces the sampled counter-tangent/load gate with one route-selected posterior amplitude-relief mechanism. I’m updating the durable lesson with the inherited v31 gate-occupancy evidence, which sharpens why instantaneous yaw moment should not be reused as a multiplicative selector.

The policy diff against evaluated v24 is deliberately narrow: one parameter-owned `0.18` relief envelope and one body-frame state-feedback modulation; outside that path the controller is unchanged. I’m invoking the required check-runner now while I independently audit schema and mechanism bounds.

The required runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account—the same infrastructure limitation recorded in inherited iterations. I’m running its exact prescribed checks directly and will record that distinction in the notes.

The substantive guidance and boundary/schema checks pass, but the guidance checker cannot identify the parent because `README.md` lists the same copied optimizer twice. I’m removing only the duplicate parent marker—an inherited rendering defect—then rerunning the prescribed checks.

The two executable prescribed checks now pass. Julia is not installed, so the runtime smoke command cannot start; I’m compensating with the deterministic schema guard, solver-boundary check, forbidden-state scan, and a structural diff against evaluated v24. The new wave gain is algebraically confined to `[0.82, 1]` before inherited smooth command projection.

Validation is complete: exactly one nonempty solver candidate exists; material-guidance, solver-boundary, and parameter-schema checks pass. The configured runner itself remains unavailable because of its pinned model, and Julia is absent, so no runtime smoke or CFD was run.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:8) — route-selected posterior half-cycle amplitude relief.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) — visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and validation.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:46) — materially revised reusable lesson.

Guidance, boundary, schema, and single-candidate checks pass. The pinned check-runner model and Julia executable were unavailable. No CFD was run.
